findings.title: New backupStatusTitle has no test; three-way title branch unpinned
findings.why_it_matters: Slack, ntfy and Telegram notifications now all take their status title from one new function, but nothing asserts which title each (succeeded, failed) pair yields. Swapping the `failed > 0 && succeeded > 0` and default cases, or corrupting the emoji constants (two of them carry an invisible U+FE0F prefix), would ship wrong notification titles with every suite still green. A small table test over the three branches would cover all three notifiers, since all of them now route through this function.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a table-driven TestBackupStatusTitle in internal/ covering (1,0)->titleBackupsSucceeded, (1,1)->titleBackupsErrors, (0,1)->titleBackupsFailed and (0,0)->titleBackupsFailed. Assert against the literal expected strings rather than the constants, so a constant edit is also caught.

go test ./internal/ -coverprofile: notify.go backupStatusTitle 0.0%, sendTelegramMessage 0.0%, sendNtfy 0.0%, sendSlackMessage 0.0%
grep of internal/*_test.go finds no reference to backupStatusTitle, titleBackups*, or the 'soba backups' titles

findings.title: Extracted provider credential checks lack partial-config and blank-value tests
findings.why_it_matters: The PR states behaviour is unchanged, but the offline suite never runs the error branches of the extracted checkJustTokenProvider (66.7%) and checkUserAndPasswordProvider (57.1%). Those branches are the 'parameter X is not defined' messages shown to users who set only some Azure DevOps or BitBucket credentials, or a blank token. Moving the `foundCount == totalCount` return or the partial-error loop during this decomposition could break startup validation unnoticed. The only existing test, TestCheckProvidersFailureWhenNoneDefined, covers the no-providers path only.
findings.suggested_fix: Add table-driven tests for checkProvider and checkProvidersDefined using t.Setenv. Cases: blank GITHUB_TOKEN yields a 'parameter ... is not defined' error; Azure DevOps with only the user name set yields an error naming the missing PAT and a count of 0; full Azure DevOps credentials yield (1, nil); full BitBucket API-token plus OAuth credentials count as one provider.

residual_risks: collectProviderBackupResults replaces five if-blocks with a table of {env var, run func}; it is 0% covered offline, so a mis-paired entry (for example Gitea mapped to the GitHub runner) would only surface in live-provider tests, which skip without credentials.

displayStartupConfig and the extracted logProvider* helpers show 100% line coverage for the entry function, but no test asserts the emitted log text. The PR claim that log output is unchanged rests on manual comparison; I compared by reading the diff and the messages and order are identical (including the 'Gitlab backup LFS' casing and the 'Organistations' typo).
testing_gaps: validateStartupConfig error paths (missing backup dir, GITHUB_ORGS without a token, nonexistent dir, stat failure) are not individually tested; only the undefined backup-dir case is reached, via TestFailureIfGitBackupDirUndefined.

createWorkingDir, scheduleBackups and runScheduledJob (the interval and cron branches and the 'failed to create job' error) are 0% covered offline. The interval/cron branches block on waitForShutdown, which makes them hard to test without injecting a signal.
The removal of TestPublicGitLabRepositoryBackup2 is sound: the diff shows its body was identical to TestPublicGitLabRepositoryBackup, so no coverage is lost.
TestGiteaOrgsRepositoryBackup helper extraction preserves assertions; resetBackups() remains called redundantly inside the switch arms and again after the switch, as it did before.
